Reference number: POC-92D596C7F2-83353  
Requested service: Lumbar disc surgery/decompression  
CPT: 63030  
Denial date: August 3, 2026

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030, lower-back disc surgery/decompression. The denial states that the submitted documentation was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. The clinical record supports medical necessity and addresses the relevant history, failed conservative treatment, objective imaging, neurologic findings, and functional impairment.

I have experienced progressive lower-back pain for 18 months. The pain has not been relieved by rest and is accompanied by radicular pain extending into the right calf. I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes, demonstrating substantial functional impairment.

The condition has persisted despite substantial conservative treatment:

- I completed 16 supervised physical-therapy visits over eight weeks, from April 14, 2026, through June 9, 2026. Treatment included core stabilization and lumbar-flexibility exercises. The physical-therapy discharge note documents this course.
- I used NSAIDs for eight months with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on April 29, 2026, provided only two weeks of partial relief.

The June 16, 2026 lumbar MRI provides objective anatomic evidence correlating with my symptoms and examination. It shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral-recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.

The examination also supports the requested surgery. There was positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. These findings match the right-sided radicular symptoms and the L5 nerve-root compression shown on MRI.

The record does not identify clinical circumstances that would otherwise prevent the requested treatment. There is no active infection or untreated substance use. My BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker.

The requested procedure is being recommended by Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery, to address the L4-L5 disc extrusion, severe lateral-recess stenosis, and L5 nerve-root compression after failure of conservative care. The duration and progression of symptoms, failed treatment, objective imaging, neurologic findings, and functional limitations together provide a complete basis for evaluating medical necessity.

Please reverse the denial and approve CPT 63030. If MedStar Family Choice DC continues to find the submission incomplete, please identify each specific missing document or clinical fact required for review rather than issuing a general incomplete-documentation denial. Please also provide the exact utilization-management criteria applied to this request, including the applicable version and effective date, and explain how the submitted records did not satisfy those criteria. The publicly available MedStar materials do not provide CPT 63030-specific medical-necessity criteria, so no plan policy language is quoted in this appeal.

Enclosed are the supporting records:

1. Lumbar MRI report dated June 16, 2026;
2. Physical-therapy discharge note documenting 16 visits from April 14, 2026, through June 9, 2026;
3. Medication and conservative-treatment history documenting eight months of NSAID use;
4. Corticosteroid-injection record dated April 29, 2026;
5. Orthopedic surgical evaluation and recommendation by Lindqvist, MD;
6. Neurologic and provocative examination findings;
7. The August 3, 2026 adverse benefit determination.

Please acknowledge receipt of this appeal and issue a written decision. If a peer-to-peer discussion or additional information from Lindqvist, MD, would assist your review, please contact the surgeon promptly.

Sincerely,
